subject: DPA incident sync & subproc dataflow — notification cadence proposal
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security@blueridge.com, m.patel@blueridge.com, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@barristerllp.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA incident sync & subproc dataflow — notification cadence proposal

Team / BlueRidge,

Following this morning's discovery call, I'm proposing a short, concrete notification cadence and handoff plan we can offer BlueRidge for section 8 (incident notification) in the DPA. The goal is to make the contract language align with our operational capabilities so we can meet SLAs without overpromising.

High-level proposal (attached redline + matrix):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 24 hours of detection with high-level scope (affected service, suspected vector, high-level data types).
- Substantive notification: within 72 hours with preliminary impact, classification (PHI/PII/system logs), and next steps.
- Forensic export window: preserve raw telemetry & KV cache snapshots for at least 90 days; coordinate export within 7 business days for prioritized requests.
- Subprocessor cooperation: we will require subprocessors to provide evidence access and export support under our DPA; where legal restrictions apply (local law), we'll provide a redacted evidentiary package and a migration plan.

Open items I want the legal and ops teams to weigh in on:
1) Is 24-hour ack safe to promise for all incident classes, or should we limit that to incidents with confirmed customer impact?
2) For cross-border evidence exports, what language keeps us compliant while still meeting a customer expectation for evidence?
3) Subprocessor notice: do we need a separate contractual push to subprocessors (i.e., contract amendment) or can we rely on current flow-down obligations?

Attached: DPA_section_8_redline.pdf (redline showing proposed language), forensic_requirements_matrix.xlsx (what we can deliver by timeline), preservation_notice_template.docx.

Next step: propose a 30-minute sync Monday to finalize language we can give BlueRidge this week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: DPA_section_8_redline.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, security@blueridge.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA incident sync & subproc dataflow — notification cadence proposal

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear proposal. A couple quick operational notes from the ops/forensics side:

- 24-hour ack: we can promise an ack in 24 hours for incidents that are either (a) detected by Redwood monitoring with a customer impact flag or (b) reported by the customer and triaged as potential data exposure. For internal detection-only telemetry anomalies (no sign of exfil), our SOC workflow typically requires up to 48 hours to validate before an external ack.

- 72-hour substantive: workable, but the 'preliminary impact' field should be narrowly defined to prevent over-commitment. Suggest: 'data classes likely involved' + 'affected model/service' + 'whether we initiated containment measures'.

- Forensic export window: 90 days preservation is fine; exports (e.g., full KV cache snapshots) can be heavy. We should offer a prioritized export for named custodians within 7 business days, and a full export SLA of 30 business days for legal requests (with expedited path for regulatory demands).

- Subprocessors: operationally, we can demand cooperation but some cloud infra subprocessors have legal constraints on cross-border exports. We should add an explicit 'if subprocessors cannot export due to local law, Redwood will provide a verified, time-stamped forensic report and redacted artifacts' clause.

I'll mark up the matrix with capacity constraints and data volumes — attaching notes in the drive.

-Ben
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: forensic_requirements_matrix.xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@barristerllp.com>, security@blueridge.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA incident sync & subproc dataflow — notification cadence proposal

Vanessa / Ben / BlueRidge counsel —

Quick legal read and suggested edits (high level):

1) 24-hour 'ack' — redline to condition the 24-hour ack on 'reasonable evidence of customer data access or confirmed service impact'. This protects us from promising a public notification for internal triage-only anomalies.

2) 72-hour substantive — retain but add: "substantive notification is subject to reasonable operational and legal constraints; Redwood will provide updates as material facts become available." That gives us flexibility for complex international incidents.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border evidence — proposed contract language:
   - Redwood will require subprocessors to cooperate reasonably with forensic investigations and evidence exports, subject to applicable law and contractual restrictions.
   - Where a subprocessor's local law prevents transfer of raw evidence, Redwood will provide certified extracts or contemporaneously-signed forensic summaries prepared by the subprocessor and supervised by Redwood's IR team.

4) Preservation and custody: add an explicit clause that Redwood may require time-limited preservation holds on specific customer artifacts and will notify affected customers of the scope and duration of the preservation hold.

5) Escalation path: add a CISO/General Counsel escalation clause for high-severity incidents (severity levels 1 or 2) that commits to a named Redwood escalation lead and weekly status calls until resolved.

Attached is a short redline with suggested phrasing (I left placeholders for service names and severity definitions). If BlueRidge wants to keep tighter SLA buckets, we can propose a two-tier approach (public sector vs. commercial).

-Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: DPA_section_8_redline.pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security@blueridge.com, m.patel@blueridge.com, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@barristerllp.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA incident sync & subproc dataflow — notification cadence proposal

Thanks all — good alignment. Summary of agreed approach we can present to BlueRidge tomorrow:

- Initial acknowledgment: within 24 hours, conditioned on reasonable evidence of customer impact.
- Substantive update: within 72 hours with narrow fields (data class, affected service, containment steps). Further investigative results will be provided iteratively.
- Preservation: Redwood will preserve telemetry and KV cache snapshots for 90 days by default and place targeted legal holds on custodian artifacts as requested.
- Export & evidence: prioritized named-custodian exports within 7 business days; full exports up to 30 business days. Where local law prevents raw export, Redwood will supply certified extracts and a signed forensic summary.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will enforce cooperation obligations; if subprocessors cannot export raw evidence due to law, the certified-extract path applies. We will also propose a clean-up clause for any subprocessor-delivered evidence to ensure no customer data is retained beyond allowed windows.
- Escalation: severity 1/2 -> Redwood CISO + GC weekly calls until remediation; named contacts to be included in the SOW.

Action items:
- Laura: finalize redline language for section 8 + preservation hold clause by EOD Tuesday. (Elena, feel free to suggest any jurisdictional edits.)
- Ben: finalize matrix with capacity/volume constraints and expected export sizes; mark which exports require legal approval.
- I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call with BlueRidge tomorrow at 10am PT and circulate the redline and matrix.

If there's anything missing, flag now. Otherwise I'll send the package to BlueRidge and Elena at 10:00am PT.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: DPA_section_8_redline.pdf; forensic_requirements_matrix.xlsx; preservation_notice_template.docx)
